gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Elite Screens says its Tripod Series ($142, ChatGPT's 'best for presentations' pick) is 'Not compatible with Ultra/Short-throw Projectors', while Elite lists the Yard Master 2 for UST, short and standard throw projectors and sells a separate UST-only tripod (Light-On CLR 3, $269).
standout_why: I opened ProjectorVerdict's tripod screen guide (projectorverdict.com/best/best-tripod-projector-screen/). It covers the Elite Tripod Series' aspect ratios and its keystone eliminator, but it never mentions throw compatibility for any pick. ProjectorVerdict's main screen guide lists UST exclusions only for the Spectrum 2, Aeon CLR 3 and CineGrey 3D, not for the Tripod. It covers the Yard Master 2's 7 mph wind limit and the WraithVeil Dual's rear projection, but not which models the extension legs fit. iTechGuides' outdoor screen guide names no throw limits and no accessory part numbers, and only tells readers to 'check the projector's throw requirements'. I couldn't read Wirecutter, the only cited page: the proxy returned HTTP 403. Esquire blocked the fetch. ChatGPT's own answer recommends the Elite Tripod without any throw warning.
decides: This confirms the Yard Master 2 as the portable pick that works with any projector throw. It disqualifies the Elite Tripod for anyone pairing it with an ultra-short-throw or short-throw portable projector; for those shoppers, the throw-safe tripod alternative is Elite's Tripod Light-On CLR 3 (UST-only). If the Yard Master 2 needs to sit higher for a group, the ZOMS2-LEGS fit only the 75–135" models, and the 58" needs different bars. Elite says neither part fits the Yard Master Plus.

findings.label: Projector throw compatibility
findings.value: Not compatible with ultra-short-throw or short-throw projectors; compatible with standard ('long') throw and triple-laser projectors
findings.source_title: Tripod Series Portable Projection Screen – Elite Screens
findings.note: Maker page says 'Not Compatible With Ultra-short/Short Throw Projectors'. The shop listing (shop.elitescreens.com/products/elite-screen-tripod) says the same: 'Not compatible with Ultra/Short-throw Projectors'.

findings.label: Formats, material and model numbers
findings.value: 16:9 from 60" to 120" (T60UWH to T120UWH), 4:3 at 84", 100" and 120" (e.g. T100UWV1, T120UWV1), 1:1 from 71" to 136". MaxWhite 2 matte white, 1.1 gain, 180° viewing angle, front projection only, built-in keystone eliminator
findings.source_title: Tripod Series Portable Projection Screen – Elite Screens
findings.note: The maker page's size selector and spec list disagree slightly on the size ranges. The ranges above come from the spec list on the shop listing.

findings.label: Carrying bag

findings.note: The maker's FAQ says a bag is not standard, but the shop spec list says a 'Fabric carrying bag included'. Elite contradicts itself, so confirm with Elite before telling shoppers the bag is included.

findings.label: Extension legs compatibility
findings.value: ZOMS2-LEGS ($56, 2 legs, adds more than 27") fits only OMS 75–135 H2/HR2/HR3/H2-DUAL (E, H, L types). The 58" OMS58H2 needs ZOMS58H2-LEGS bars (17"). Elite says neither fits Yard Master PLUS screens

findings.label: Replacement screen material
findings.value: Z-OMSxxxH2 CineWhite UHD-B front material, $167.00, fits Yard Master 2 OMSxxxH2 only; 'Not compatible with Yard Master plus series'. Plus-series materials ($293) are 'Not compatible with Yard Master series'
findings.source_title: [Elite Screens] Yard Master 2 - Screen Material | CineWhite UHD-B (Front Projection)
findings.note: Elite requires the screen's model and serial number with the order, or the order is cancelled automatically.

findings.label: Stakes and rope exclusion; wind limit
findings.value: Stakes, rope and support rings included except on OMS55HR2 and OMS58H2; light breeze only, up to 7 mph

findings.note: The maker page's FAQ gives 10 mph as the point where damage can occur, so Elite contradicts itself. ProjectorVerdict already reports the 7 mph limit.
